trickyParts: A job holding contents: write, packages: write, id-token: write, attestations: write or the deploy key runs no script of this repository (.github/scripts/check-release-credentials.sh:230 refuses any scripts/ path but release-push.sh), so every credentialed job reads the derived value from an upstream job's output. GitHub's needs context is not transitive, so docker, image_index, attest and release_publish each name targets in their own needs; release_publish's if: uses always(), so it also tests needs.targets.result.
release-envoy-listener.yaml's targets job became a build job by running a script, so check-release-credentials.sh requires it to end in the release-push.sh no-credential tripwire.

worker-image.yaml's attest job runs with build skipped in an attest-only call, so it cannot read needs.build.outputs: the new optional workflow_call input image is what release.yaml's worker_image_attest passes, and subject-name is ${{ inputs.image || needs.build.outputs.image }}.

plugin_download_url ends in the literal ${VERSION}, Pulumi's own placeholder. It survives the command substitution, the $GITHUB_ENV round trip, the single-quoted -X argument and jq's --arg; the release smoke test now compares against the derived value, and ci.yaml's envoy-smoke step holds the literal cybermonklabs address, which is what pins the script's output.

The equivalence is read-side only. internal/record/store.go is untouched: a record's repository is immutable (store.go:213, :224-227), so a tree keeps the name it was recorded under for its whole life and the pair must stay configured for as long as any record names the old repository. That is said in legion.yaml.example, in --check-config's line and in AGENTS.md.

The served set stays Dispatch's mapping. A rename adds no repository and reads nothing from GitHub, because nameAccepted's read fails the whole mapping read on the first repository GitHub cannot answer, and a pair configured before the transfer names a repository GitHub does not have yet. A configured pair whose `to` the project does not serve is logged once at the boot's mapping load.

Three reads of the pull_requests table are keyed on its repo column with plain SQL equality (record/store.go's PullRequestByNumber, PullRequestByBranch and PullRequestRecorded). The reviewers' pass found that a pull request already open at the transfer is reached by none of them under the new name, which is exactly the parent issue's acceptance, so Engine.pullRequest, Engine.pullRequestByBranch, internal/daemon's reviewedRepository and intake's recordedPullRequest now read through ghrepo.Renames.Lookups: the name, then the pair's other name, one extra query only when the first finds nothing, and exactly one query for a deployment that configures no rename.

The same pass found that outbox.checkDeployRun compared GitHub's run.HeadRepository.FullName — the repository's CURRENT name — with check.Repo by EqualFold, which would have refused every deploy run after a transfer and silently left the production check unwoken. The outbox now carries the equivalence.

The gh bundle, not the directory, is what moves: a pod's GH_CONFIG_DIR is fixed at launch from its issue's recorded owner, and ghconfig.WriteBundle deletes every directory the bundle does not name, so pointing the lookup at the new owner's directory would break every live pod. Instead a renamed pair gets one entry, minted for the owner the repository moved to, written into both owners' directories, carrying the write lease whenever either owner is the bundle's Default. legion gh, legion git-credential and both runtimes are unchanged.
deviations: Acceptance 4 is met by the token rather than by the directory, as the plan's B-D3 decided and recorded as a spec departure for the architect: a tree under sjawhar/legion keeps its own gh directory and that directory holds the cybermonklabs owner's write token. The test asserts the token.

The plan did not name the four pull-request lookups keyed on the repo column, nor outbox.checkDeployRun. Both are defects this change would otherwise have left — the first is the parent issue's own acceptance that a tree open at the transfer keeps working — so both are fixed here, with tests.
